New Kid's Box focus: Back to school!

Learn classroom words, count from 11 to 20, and talk about what is or is not in a classroom.

How many books are there? There are twelve books.
Is there a ruler on the desk? Yes, there is.
Are there nineteen pens? No, there aren't.

About 30 minutes a day

Monday–Friday home routine

New Unit 2 content stays the main focus. Short review blocks keep last week's weaker skills connected instead of dropping them.

Mon

School words + F f

  • 10 min School vocabulary: listen, point, say.
  • 5 min Numbers 11–15.
  • 4 min Puzzle Words: she, be.
  • 3 min Handwriting F f.
  • 8 min Read Will Is Up at Bat.
Tue

There is / are + G g

  • 10 min There is / There are with school words.
  • 5 min Numbers 16–20.
  • 4 min Puzzle Words: theirs, me.
  • 3 min Handwriting G g.
  • 8 min Read I Like Soccer.
Wed

Long ee + H h

  • 8 min Long ee: bee, see, green, tree.
  • 5 min Quick wh retrieval.
  • 5 min A–Z capital/small + letter sound check.
  • 4 min Puzzle Words: them, I.
  • 3 min Handwriting H h.
  • 5 min Read I Can Mix Colors.
Thu

Is there? / Are there? + I i

  • 8 min Ask and answer classroom questions.
  • 3 min Quick Mr / Mrs review: man or married woman?
  • 4 min Character names + he/she dictation.
  • 4 min Puzzle Words: they, he.
  • 3 min Handwriting I i.
  • 8 min Re-read the hardest one so far: Will Is Up at Bat, I Like Soccer, or I Can Mix Colors.
Fri

Mixed review + J j

  • 10 min Exam Master mixed Unit 2 + old review.
  • 5 min Puzzle Words: you, we + dictation.
  • 3 min Handwriting J j.
  • 5 min Saturday food-expression practice.
  • 7 min Choose one Week 2 Flyleaf reader and re-read it smoothly; if time, start a second.
Unit 2 vocabulary

School words · See, hear, say

Picture rule: official Kid's Box flashcards are used first. Clear real-photo references are used only where the Level 2 flashcard set has no matching card.

New Unit 2 names

Number reading

Numbers 11–20

Look at the number, say the number word, then press 🔊 Hear if you want to check your reading.

Read aloud

Sentence reading

Try to read each sentence by yourself first. Then press 🔊 Listen to check that you read it correctly.

There is a ruler on the desk.
There are twelve books in the bookcase.
There isn't a TV.
There aren't nineteen pens.
Pink-page Puzzle Words · page 2

See/read → hear → hide → write on paper → check

Do not type these words. Read the word, hear it, hide it, write it on paper from memory, then reveal it and check your own spelling.

Separate Puzzle Word dictation

For next week's spelling: press one number. You will hear the whole word first, then each lowercase letter slowly with about a 1.5-second pause. Write the word on paper. Use Check words only after you have finished.

One letter each day. Write the capital and small letter several times on lined paper.

Next Saturday speaking practice

Food expressions · same meaning, more natural English

Listen to the whole question, choose the sentence with nearly the same meaning, then say the correct expression aloud.

Remember our funny choice: “I’m a sour person.” Sour describes a taste here; it does not mean “I love sweet food.”

Speaking follow-up

What food are you a fan of?
What is your favourite food?
What do you prefer to something else?
What food are you not a fan of?
Do you have a sweet tooth?
What is your go-to snack?
